CB30: Three decades of history

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
unimaginable changes have taken place in South Africa and internationally since you first heard our signature tune way back in 1988

Unique Selling Point:
Carte Blanche has covered many of history's triumphs and tragedies. At a time when populists are trying to rewrite our history we go back to show you how your wolrld has changed

Summary:
In 1988 South Africa was a very different country. President PW Botha was state president, Nelson Mandela was behind bars, townships were on fire, and activists resisted a repressive state of emergency. The idea of Nelson Mandela as president six years later, was as alien to some as the idea of a black president of the United States. There was no internet, cell phones or even email and we had no idea that a young man from South Africa would make himself a billionaire and fund his way into space.

Further information:
Wars, the rise of global terrorism, natural disasters - Carte Blanche has been on the frontlines covering these events - and recording the lives of the hero's and the villains creating history

Script:


Final script Epic moments TX 26th August

Commentary One
For the last three decades you have travelled the road with us through triumph and tragedy, good times and bad, as our brief history in time, unfolded

Up sound De Klerk Parliament

In 1990 FW De Klerk, unbanned the ANC, released Nelson Mandela and changed South Africa's political trajectory

FW DE Klerk
We had failed to bring justice and the challenge was to do what is right!

Commentary two
Our first broadcast in 1988 was to a very different country. PW Botha was in charge, and the townships were on fire.

Up sound guns

Nelson Mandela was behind bars, and activists resisted a repressive state of emergency

Up sound Desmond Tutu
If I was not able to attract the media how were we going to be able to tell the world of the viciousness of the system?!

Commentary three
30 years later, some sneer when we call our transition a miracle, but we forget the Boipatong massacre, Chris Hani's assassination and how close to civil war we came.

Ruda
Nelson Mandela appealed to the nation to choose peace not war

Commentary Four
We covered the insults, anger and suspicion as our leaders kept talking at Codesa and began to dismantle the apartheid machinery

Mandela
He has very little idea what democracy means

Commentary Five
Somehow democracy prevailed - and our peaceful elections of 1994 defied the doomsayers

Bomb explodes Rwanda up sound

Commentary six
But 1994 was also Rwanda's darkest hour.

Up Sound Ruda

Commentary seven
And in Europe, ethnic cleansing in Bosnia shocked the world. We joined Englishwomen Sally Trench helping victims in 1995

Derek
In this area, hardly a building has been left intact, there is a putrid smell in the air. You can only imagine how much blood has been spilt, how many lives have been lost, how many families obliterated in this street alone

Commentary eight
In 1996 we began to seek restorative justice at the Truth and reconciliation commission
Poet Antjie Krog covered the daily horrors

Up sound Ruda reads Antjie Krog
For me this crying is the beginning of the Truth commission- the signature tune the definitive moment, the ultimate sound of what the process is all about …finding words for that cry of Nomonde Calata

Commentary nine
President Thabo Mbeki began his term in 1999 with calls for a new world order responsive to the needs of the poor, but his stance on aids and Zimbabwe marred his presidency. Soon our northern neighbor became a failed state

Up sound lightning and thunder

Commentary ten
But the storms across our borders weren't all political.

Up sound helicopter

Mozambicans remember the floods of 2000 and 2001

Derek
Tens of thousands of Mozambicans poorest people are running from water …they leave behind them their homes, their crops and their livelihoods

Up sound Volcano

Commentary Eleven
A few months later a Volcano erupted in eastern DRC

Ruda
The volcano cut the town in half ….ending in lake Kivu

Up sound Tsunami happening

Commentary Twelve
Further afield Derek met survivors of the 2011 earthquake and Tsunami in Japan.

Derek Link
This used to be a suburb…..now its just a checkerboard of foundations and streets

Commentary Thirteen
But not long after we celebrated the new century, a Tsunami of a different kind, would change the world. Global terrorism was on the rise- and America was a prime target

Up sound 911 buildings plane hits

Commentary fourteen
Random acts of global terror spread into Africa. In Kenya we came face to face with its terrible impact.

Up sound Kenyan shopping mall

Commentary fifteen
We have followed our fair share of wars. In 1993 Mogadishu in Somalia erupted

Up sound
Be careful they are shooting straight at us

Commentary sixteen
After 911, America wanted revenge. Under a pretext of weapons of mass destruction - they bombed Iraq and deposed Saddam Hussain.

Aircraft takes off from carrier

Commentary Seventeen
We reported from the USS George Washington in the gulf

Derek
The main strike power of the George Washington is carrier airwing 1 which boasts more than 70 aircraft on board

Commentary eighteen
Meanwhile Africa's great war, largely under reported, happened right on our doorstep.

John up sound
The frontline is about an hour's flight north of here and that is where we are heading now

Commentary nineteen
As many as 5 million people may have died in the Congo war of 1998 to 2002.
Today South Africa's military plays an integral role, as part of the UN Peacekeepers

Jacob Zuma
Umshimiwam!

Commentary twenty
But as battles go- here on home soil, an epic one was playing out for the highest office in the land. Jacob Zuma versus Thabo Mbeki. But in 2006 Jacob Zuma had a set back

John
Jacob Zuma is on trial for rape

Commentary Twenty- one
Acquitted on the rape charges, and with corruption in the arms deal charges dropped, Zuma was unstoppable, and in 2009 he became South Africa's third democratically elected president.

Up sound shooting Marikana

Commentary Twenty- two
But the Marikana massacre three years later, painted a picture of a heartless government that could mow down poor mine workers wanting a better wage

Julius
We are going to change the dress code of that parliament

Commentary Twenty -three
Marikana also provided a perfect platform for Jacob Zuma's former praise singer Julius Malema, who left the ANC, founded the EFF then turned on Zuma, and caused havoc in Parliament

Up sound fighters in the house -pay back the money

Commentary Twenty -four
By December that same year Africa's greatest statesman Nelson Mandela drew his last breath, and the first black president of the United states travelled to Johannesburg to pay his respects

Commentary Twenty- five
But the hope inspired by Mandela, was squandered during Jacob Zuma's presidency, which became synonymous with state capture and late- night cabinet reshuffles for those who opposed him

Bongani to Pravin
How were you told
Pravin
I wasn't told I learnt through a tv screen.
Bongani
That's extraordinary
Pravin
That's life

Commentary Twenty-six
An estimated R100 billion rand was funneled out of the fiscus, and the economy brought to the edge of junk. But South Africans fought back.

Vavi up sound
We are up to here with their corruption

Commentary Twenty-seven
Sunday after Sunday, as the battle for the soul of South Africa waged, we brought you
Nkandla, the Gupta wedding, Estina dairy, SARS, the NPA, Eskom, PRASA, Esidemeni, Bell Pottinger, KMPG, and that was just the half of it

Up sound of Hoes! Hoes!

Commentary Twenty- eight
For almost a decade our public life has swung between order and chaos. Incredible South African's rose up to resist the rot, speaking truth to power

Makhosi Khoza
Please Mr President step down and respect those who elected you.

Commentary Twenty-nine
Now in this so called new dawn, it's those stories we will continue to tell.

THE END
PROMO ONE
For three decades Carte Blanche has been on the frontlines as our country has changed beyond recognition. From PW Botha to the years of state capture under President Zuma, we take you through some of the most epic moments

PROMO TWO
The rise of global terrorism, inclement weather political triumph and turmoil, we go back into our archives

Bongani to Pravin
How were you told
Pravin
I wasn't told I learnt through a tv screen.
Bongani
That's extraordinary
Pravin
That's life
